rules.statement: When a CIBA request is denied, notify a ping or push client exactly once, and only from the call whose own update of the grant decided the request; a call that finds the request already decided dispatches nothing.
rules.why: If every denial call sent a notification, a concurrent decision would notify the client twice. Without any notification, a ping or push client waits until the request expires.
rules.check: Look for a CIBA denial path, including the denial of a refused approval, that never dispatches a ping/push notification. Also look for one that dispatches without checking that its own state update decided the request.

rules.statement: A CIBA push-mode denial notification carries `auth_req_id` and `error` set to `access_denied`, with no tokens and no `error_description`. A ping-mode denial carries only `auth_req_id`, and the token endpoint answers `access_denied` when the client polls.
rules.why: CIBA Core 1.0 §10.2 and §12 define these payloads. `error_description` is optional, and the end user may not be the party that denied the request.
rules.check: Look for push denial payloads that include tokens or an error_description, and for ping denial bodies that carry anything beyond auth_req_id.

rules.statement: Do not send a callback notification to a CIBA poll-mode client on denial; it learns the denial from the token endpoint.
rules.why: Poll clients have no callback, and the token endpoint reports the denial.
rules.check: Look for denial notifications dispatched without first checking that the client uses ping or push delivery mode.

rules.statement: Send CIBA denial notifications through the same durable, retrying delivery job that carries approvals, and have the job carry only the error code and no tokens.
rules.why: Denials then get the same retries as every delivery, and a durable dispatcher never persists tokens for a denial.
rules.check: Look for denial notifications sent by a direct HTTP call that skips the delivery job, and for denial jobs that carry token data.
